description: VIS is Euclid's visible camera. It uses one broad band, I_E, covering roughly the combined r, i and z range. The instrument paper plots the optical throughput and CCD detective quantum efficiency and states a 550–920 nm passband. No separate VIS numerical throughput file is listed on the ESA Euclid reference-data site.
short_description: Euclid VIS visible camera broad band I_E
facility_description: Euclid is an ESA visible and near-infrared space survey, launched on 1 July 2023, with a 1.20 m Korsch off-axis three-mirror telescope.
notes: The arXiv record for Cropper et al. links the article to the CC BY 4.0 deed (license icon by-4.0.png, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The deed page also says: "This deed highlights only some of the key features and terms of the actual license. It is not a license and has no legal value." The quoted Share sentence is the redistribution statement on that deed. No VIS throughput file appears on https://euclid.esac.esa.int/msp/refdata/, which says the archived items are Mission Reference Data V1.0 (draft), NISP photometric passbands (V1.0) and a planetary nebulae spectral atlas (V1.0). The passband edges are not the same in every opened source: Cropper et al. use 550–920 nm, while the Euclid Consortium overview says "single passband: I E =530-920nm" and the NISP instrument paper says "VIS has one single wide passband between ∼530 and 920 nm". The NISP product acknowledgement was not copied onto VIS. The archive-wide Euclid credit line on the ESA terms page was not attached, because no VIS numerical product was found in the archive. Q1 data-credit text was not used.

vis.Description: Single broad VIS band I_E. Cropper et al. give the passband as 550–920 nm and describe it as approximately r+i+z. Figure 7 shows optical-element throughput, CCD detective quantum efficiency, and the total throughput.
